shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away A for B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety (1,1,1 -> 0,1,2), which lowers my utility since I value variety equally across goods.
Trading B for A would just shift me from equal 1-1-1 holdings to 2 A/0 B, reducing variety and not improving utility since I value balanced holdings.

Giving up my only B to get 2 more A would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, which hurts variety since I value having a balanced spread of goods. I'd rather negotiate a trade that keeps some B while gaining A.
Trading away my only C to get a second B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 2 B, reducing variety and utility since I already value diversity. Not beneficial.

This would give me 2C, 0B, 1A - moving from balanced (1,1,1) to unbalanced holdings reduces variety value. Trading 1B for 1C just shifts my imbalance without net gain since I'd go from equal distribution to having none of B.
Giving up my only B to get more C would hurt variety since I'd end up with 0 B and 3 C, reducing overall balance in my bundle.

This trade would give me 2B/0A, reducing variety (1,1,1 to 0,2,1), which decreases my utility since I value balanced holdings. I'd rather keep my even distribution or trade for something that doesn't zero out a good.

Giving up my only B to get more A (which I already have) would leave me with zero variety in B, hurting my balanced preference. I'd rather negotiate a trade that keeps some B while still gaining A or C.

Trading 1C for 1B would leave me with 0C, 1A, 2B, reducing variety. Since I currently have equal amounts of all goods (1 each), giving up a good I only have one of to get a duplicate good would decrease my utility due to the variety preference.

This trade would leave me with 0 C and 0 B, over-concentrating in A, which hurts my variety-based utility. I'd prefer a trade that balances my holdings across C, A, and B instead.

Giving away my only B (going to 0) while having 2 A and 0 C would leave me with 2A,1C,0B - trading one scarce good for another scarce good doesn't improve variety balance. I'd rather keep B and seek C from elsewhere without depleting B entirely.
Trading my single B for 2C improves variety balance: moving from (C0,A2,B1) to (C2,A2,B0) increases overall diminishing-returns utility since C was previously at zero.
